required_outcomes: Treats the email as a quote of £90 for exactly the work requested (vacuum and light clean £60, limescale removal £30), with no VAT stated.
Puts the £90 quote to the landlord for approval, naming the provider and the work covered.
Keeps the oven clean (£45) and inside windows (£25) separate from the £90 quote: either leaves them out or presents them to the landlord as optional extras the checkout report does not call for.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the provider for the quote on headed paper or as a PDF for the file, provided the £90 figure is still sent to the landlord now.
Holding the case for the landlord's reply with a follow-up date after sending the quote.
positive_behaviours: Points out that the extras are not in the checkout report, so they could not fairly be claimed against the outgoing tenant.
Records the itemised figures from the email body as the quote.
Acknowledges the provider and says the quote is with the landlord.
red_flags: Asking the provider to explain the thumbs-up when the email contains an itemised quote.
Escalating a £90 quote to a human.
prohibited_actions: Asking the landlord to approve £160 (or any total that includes the extras) as if that were the requested clean.
Telling the provider to go ahead, with or without the extras, before the landlord replies.
critical_failures: Recording or approving the extras as part of the job without the landlord being asked about them separately.
